I'm personally fine with that. Action role-playing games that allow stat rerolling are usually balanced in a way that allows such a thing without making it problematic for the game as a whole.  
This specific game isn't like that, its special mod system was added upon the already existing mess. Power creep might already be a problem, but making it worse is certainly not a solution.  
Giving players a guaranteed path towards the most overpowered version possible (which stat-locking would introduce) would certainly make things worse. At least randomness keeps this problem at bay, while trade economy also benefits from scarcity.

I think these special mods are cool, they provide players an opportunity to improve a specific weapon in ways that usually wouldn't be possible, especially if it's a low tier weapon they'd like to bring into high level content. It also provides plenty of replayability thanks to cycling. And, as I have already mentioned, they seem to be beneficial for the player market.  

Perhaps ability to lock one stat would be a good compromise. But as a downside, maybe it should also render that mod untradeable.   
Couple of improvements I would personally like:  

1. Make it so the upgrade tool could be used to drop the cycling cost back to 900 once it reaches its maximum (3500), that would reduce overall resource cost for people who hunt specific bosses, I think that'd be a cool bonus for them.  

2. Replace Rifle/Shotgun/Secondary/Melee veiled mods with just one single Veiled mod type. Weapon type it would belong to upon being unveiled would depend on which weapon is used to complete its challenge. Meaning you can place it on your primary, shotgun, pistol or melee weapon, and when you unveil it, this mod will be of that weapon type.  
I agree with people when they say that there's too much RNG when it comes to these mods. I'm okay with their stats being entirely random, but I would like at least some control over them. Such as weapon type. When a specific event gives you secondary mods when all you care about are melee ones, for example, it sucks.
